title: From dictation to a brief, with nothing lost: auditable refinement

message.text: Taken: I'll build one tool, Server/refine.mjs, that turns a raw dictation into clean → structured → brief, with a coverage table showing where every sentence you said went. Three minions in sequence (the tool, then an honest audit of how the VS Code tab relayed three of your 09-28 dictations, then this card's view), in one pool worktree, about $10.

Two minions started: one builds refine.mjs, one (Opus) is reading three of your 09-28 dictations line by line and listing every ask, to check what the VS Code tab's briefs kept, changed or dropped. The card's view comes third, once both have files to show.

message.text: The tool is built, and it now also flags words you never said and sentences a brief cites but only half keeps. It's running on the three 09-28 dictations now, and the side-by-side view (raw | clean | structured | brief) is built against a test run.

A caution before the site goes on Wi-Fi: the dev server once had a command-running endpoint that anyone on the network could reach. It was closed, but only MCP.js had the loopback-only guard, so check that every Server/ route is locked to this machine before you open it to your phone.

The tool ran on all three 09-28 dictations. On the longest one, its own first brief dropped 23 of your asks (auto-compact, session forking, cost built into OpenRouter). Its coverage table caught every one, so I'm adding a repair round that puts them back in and checks again.

The repair round works: on the harness dictation, the asks the tool's first brief had dropped went from 8 to 1, for 26 cents. The audit so far: the VS Code tab dropped 4, 3 and 7 of your asks and turned several suggestions into rules, but it always passed your raw words along beside the brief.

Landed. refine.mjs is merged, and this card shows it on your three dictations beside the audit table. It went well over budget: $47 against $10, mostly two minions whose context kept growing through five Servex restarts. The next step is coverage checked per idea, not per sentence, because the audit shows the current check still misses drops inside long sentences.
